caption:
Day 5 of Watch Hunting in Tokyo takes us to Firekids in Nakano to see one fo the rarest Seikos ever.

The Seiko Astronomical Observatory Chronometer ref. 4520-8020 was built using only the 226 movements that passed the Neuchâtel Observatory most rigorous tests. This is especially important as it was the first time a non-swiss company ranked first. These movements were then cased and sold to the japanese public. We are not sure how many survived to this day but this is truly a special and rare piece.

I should clarify that there is a Seiko that is rarer. The Seiko Imperial was made for the royal family and it appears to have been donated around Europe to officials during the family’s trip in the 60s. Three have surfaced so far but it doesn’t have a liquid market to compare.

What do you think? Into it?

caption:
This vinyl cafe in Tokyo lets you pick your own record and listen at your table while sipping coffee and enjoying desserts.

It spans two floors, each with its own distinct vibe. The ground floor is bright and welcoming—great for a casual coffee break—while the basement is moodier and quieter, designed for immersive listening.

Each table has its own turntable and two headsets, perfect for sharing music with a friend. The vinyl selection includes everything from contemporary hits to timeless classics, anime soundtracks, and even K-pop.

Once inside, you’ll order a drink or dessert (around ¥600), pay a small entry fee (¥1200 on weekdays, ¥1500 on weekends), and watch a short instructional video on how to handle the records properly.

If it’s quiet, you can stay as long as you like. On busier days, they enforce a 90-minute limit to give others a chance to enjoy the space. And yes, they even have Ghibli records. transcription: Come with me to get my very first pair of Anitsuka Tigers. We went to the one in Ginza because we really wanted to get our shoes embroidered. So we took the train and we got there about an hour before the store opened. They gave us a little ticket thing to hold our place online and then we just went to explore a little bit and then came back after about an hour or two. And then it was finally my turn! I went straight downstairs. I was so so excited. When I got there it was a little busy but it started dying down after a little bit. There were so many color options and I know people tell you to kind of have an idea of what you want. but I honestly did not. And I don't think it's the end of the world if you don't either. I thought I wanted something nice and simple and neutral. But then I saw these. Like the kill build one. And I was like, wait, I did not believe in love at first sight until I put these shoes on. I got them in a size 6. So they let you do four characters. And you're also able to pick which side of your shoe you want on. And I got mine on my left. But unfortunately, you can only get it on one shoe. Then after we paid, they gave us a receipt. And then they told us to come back at 6. You'll pick them. And it was six o'clock, so it was time to go figure out my shoes. I gave them my little envelope with a receipt in it, and then they went to grab my shoes. Side note, the workers here are super nice and super helpful and patient. So in case you're nervous, don't be, they're so so nice. Anyways, I got my shoes! Quick, what do you guys think I got on mine? Three, two, one! Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa! Anyways, I was super excited about my shoes, and I still am. Overall, super fun experience. I had so much fun and I love my shoes. Did I mention I love my shoes? So if you guys are ever in Ginza, make sure to visit the store.
